subject: general
question: In an F-shaped combustion chamber, which of the following parts is generally NOT located on the extended side of the combustion chamber in a petrol engine?
solution:
The correct answer is __Camshaft.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The camshaft__ is generally NOT located on the extended side of an F-shaped combustion chamber in a petrol engine.
 
• The camshaft is responsible for controlling the opening and closing of the inlet and outlet valves.
 
• In an F-shaped combustion chamber, parts like the spark plug, inlet valve, and outlet valve are typically located on the extended side.
 
• The camshaft is usually positioned above the cylinder or within the engine block, depending on the engine design.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Function of the Camshaft:**

 
 
• The camshaft is a rotating shaft in the engine that contains cam lobes.
 
• These cam lobes push against components like valve lifters or rocker arms to open and close the valves.
 
 
 
• **Inlet and Outlet Valves:**
 
 
• The inlet valve allows the air-fuel mixture to enter the combustion chamber.
 
• The outlet valve allows exhaust gases to exit the combustion chamber.
 
 
 
• **Spark Plug:**
 
 
• The spark plug ignites the air-fuel mixture in the combustion chamber.
 
• It is typically positioned on the extended side of the F-shaped combustion chamber.
